content.rationale: The README is the repository's one front door, so it carries a title and a short introduction followed by the four sections this decision names: Getting started, Features, Development and License. The title and the introduction name the extension as uuutyrzs records it — deccy-viewer, displayed as "Deccy Viewer", a Visual Studio Code extension that visualises the deccy graph of a project — and the introduction adds the connections-between-nodes fact uuutyrzs records in its rationale, while adding nothing about installation, configuration or requirements. Each section then restates the commitment its prerequisite settles in readable, user-focused prose: Getting started names the 'Deccy: Open Deccy Graph' command on the two surfaces rzkvnnll records — the Command Palette and the editor title bar entry shown while the graph webview panel is the active webview panel — and no other way in; Features summarises oxxwkrvo's user-visible capabilities across the interactive graph panel (boxes for decisions, rounded boxes for evaluations, solid dependency edges and dashed evaluation edges each with a single arrowhead at the child end, visibly marked unresolved edges, and each node's box displaying only its label from the jj change description), text search (pressing `/` with no modifier to open a focused search field without changing selection, pan or zoom; typing a query to mark every node whose id, label or content matches case-insensitively and marking none when empty; pressing Enter and Shift+Enter to step to the next and previous marked node in graph order wrapping at either end; and pressing Esc to close the field and clear the search marks and selection), the detail panel's three labelled sections — Kind, Content and Rationale — in that fixed order with empty sections still shown with their labels, type-based formatting in the Content section while keeping its label and place and leaving Kind and Rationale unchanged (wrapped running text with paragraph breaks preserved and no code framing for narrative prose, a verbatim monospaced block labelled with the content type preserving line breaks and indentation without refusing or hiding unrecognised types for structured or code and any other content types, and the content type with referenced file paths in that block for file-referenced content), and the four labelled relationship sections — `depends_on`, `evaluates`, `dependents` and `evaluators` — listing related node ids for the selected node's prerequisites, evaluated nodes (empty for a decision), dependents and evaluators, with empty sections showing an explicit empty state, adding no unrecorded feature claims or internal schema and implementation mechanics; Development gives ynmpvmmp's single VS Code debug session from a fresh clone with no manual build, install or packaging; and License names Apache-2.0 and points readers at the repository-root LICENSE file for the full text, as rolozxtn records. Composition, not new product policy, is the commitment: each section states its prerequisite's subject without contradicting or overreaching it, leaving out installation, packaging, marketplace and troubleshooting guidance. Consistent with vqultolm and vutylkzu, the README is packaging metadata that vsce force-includes in the vsix alongside the manifest outside .vscodeignore's control, not a runtime payload file loaded by the extension.
